_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 47 (Jacob meets Pharaoh; Joseph's land policy; Jacob's deathbed instruction). Saadia-specific: v.6 'ריסא אלוכלא' = 'chiefs of stewards' for שרי מקנה; v.11 'בלד עין שמס' = 'land of Ein Shams / Heliopolis' for רעמסס (Saadia identifies); v.29 'אום בידך אלי' עהדי' = 'place your hand under my covenant' (= B24:2,9).

translations.1: And Joseph entered to Pharaoh, and told him, and said: 'My father and my brothers, and their sheep and their cattle and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of al-Sadir (Goshen).'
translations.2: And he took five men of his brothers, and presented them before Pharaoh.
translations.3: And Pharaoh said to his brothers: 'What is your occupation?' They said to him: 'Your servants are shepherds of sheep — we and our fathers.'
translations.4: Then they said: 'We have come to sojourn in your land — for there is no pasture for the sheep of your servants, because the famine is severe in the land of Canaan; let your servants dwell in the land of al-Sadir.'
translations.5: And Pharaoh said to Joseph: 'Your father and your brothers have come to you.
translations.6: Behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle them in its best part; let them dwell in the land of al-Sadir. And if you know that there are men of valor among them, set them as chiefs of stewards over my cattle.'
translations.7: And Joseph brought Jacob his father in, and set him before Pharaoh; and he greeted him.
translations.8: Pharaoh said to him: 'How many are the years of your life?'
translations.9: Jacob said to him: 'The years of my lifetime are a hundred and thirty years; few and evil have they been, and have not reached the years of the lifetime of my fathers in the days of their sojourning.'
translations.10: Then Jacob blessed him; and he went out from before him.
translations.11: And Joseph settled his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt — in its best part — that is the land of Ein Shams (Rameses) — as Pharaoh had commanded.
translations.12: And Joseph supplied his father and his brothers, and the rest of his father's household, with food — by the measure of their little ones.
translations.13: And there was no food in all the land — for the famine was very severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished from the famine.
translations.14: And Joseph gathered all the money found in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan, in exchange for the grain they bought; and he brought it into Pharaoh's treasury.
translations.15: And when the money was used up from the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying: 'Give us food — that we may not die before you; for the money is used up.'
translations.16: Joseph said to them: 'Bring your livestock; I shall give you grain for them, since the money is used up.'
translations.17: And they brought their livestock; and he gave them food for the horses, and for the flocks of sheep, and for the cattle, and for the donkeys; and he supplied them with food for all their livestock that year.
translations.18: And when that year was used up, they came to him in the second year, and said: 'We shall not hide from my lord that the money is used up, and the livestock and the beasts are with my lord; nothing remains before me except our bodies and our fields.
translations.19: Why should we die in your presence — we and our fields? Buy us and our fields for food; and we shall be servants, and our fields shall be Pharaoh's property. And give us seed, that we may live and not die, and the land may not be desolate.'
translations.20: And Joseph bought all the fields of the Egyptians for Pharaoh — for they sold them, each man his property, because the famine was severe upon them; and the lands became Pharaoh's.
translations.21: And he removed the people from their towns, from one end of Egypt's border to the other.
translations.22: Only the fields of their priests he did not buy — for the provision was theirs from Pharaoh; and they would eat their provision which he gave them; therefore they did not need to sell their fields.
translations.23: Then Joseph said to the people: 'Behold, I have bought you and your fields for Pharaoh; here is seed for you to sow in the land.
translations.24: And when the produce comes in, you shall give the fifth to Pharaoh; and the four parts shall be yours — for seed of the fields, and for food, and for those in your households, and for your little ones.'
translations.25: They said: 'You have kept us alive; we have found favor with my lord, and we shall be servants of Pharaoh.'
translations.26: And Joseph made it a statute to this day over the land of Egypt: that they should give the fifth to Pharaoh — except for the fields of the priests alone; those were theirs alone, and did not become Pharaoh's.
translations.27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of al-Sadir; and they possessed it; and they bore fruit and multiplied greatly.
translations.28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the whole of his lifetime came to a hundred and forty-seven years.
translations.29: And when the time of Israel's death drew near, he called his son Joseph, and said to him: 'If I have found favor with you, place your hand under my covenant; and do me a kindness and a favor — that you shall not bury me in Egypt.
translations.30: Rather — when I come to my fathers, carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burial-place.' He said: 'I shall do as you have said.'
translations.31: He said: 'Swear to me.' And he swore to him. And Israel bowed down upon the head of the bed in thanks.
